title: Small families of subsets: pseudointersections, maximality, and ultrafilter bases
summary: Three uncountable minima measure failures of pseudointersections, extensions of almost disjoint families, and small ultrafilter bases.
abstract: A countable family of sets of natural numbers whose every finite intersection is infinite admits an infinite set almost contained in every member: only finitely many points can fail each containment. Larger families can prevent this, and the pseudointersection number is the least size of such an obstruction. Two related minima measure the smallest infinite maximal family of infinite subsets with pairwise finite intersections, and the smallest base for a nonprincipal ultrafilter. A base supplies a subset of every member of the ultrafilter, which contains no finite sets. All three minima are uncountable and at most the size of the real line. The pseudointersection number is no larger than either the ultrafilter number or the bounding number, the least size of a family of natural-number functions with no common eventual upper bound. The bounding number is in turn no larger than the almost disjointness number. Under the continuum hypothesis all three minima equal the first uncountable cardinal.

based_on.title: Combinatorial Cardinal Characteristics of the Continuum
